money.reportActualExpensesHint: Money that went out during the selected month.

money.reportVarianceNetHint: Difference between actual net and target net.
money.reportTrendDescription: Income, expenses, and net by day for the selected month.

money.reportRootComparisonDescription: Compare root-category actuals against targets and drill into the branch.

money.reportTargetValidation: Enter an amount greater than zero.
money.reportSelfAliasesDescription: Aliases help exclude transfers to yourself when bank text uses abbreviations or alternate spellings.
money.reportAliasPlaceholder: Add alias, for example Podreshetnikov M
money.reportFxApproximateBody: Some conversions used the nearest previous FX rate because the exact date was missing.
money.reportFxMissingBody: This report cannot be calculated yet because required FX rates are missing.
money.reportLoadFailed: Could not load the budget report.
money.deleteTransactionConfirm: Delete this transaction? Line items will be removed too.
money.filtersHint: Choose accounts, categories, statuses, and ranges before applying the feed.
money.amountHint: Use negative for expenses, positive for income.
money.lineItemsMismatch: Line items total differs from transaction amount.
money.noTransactionsHint: Create your first transaction to get started.
money.importNoSourceAccounts: No {source} accounts. Add an account first.
money.importNoSourceAccountsTooltip: There are no accounts for {source}. Add one with the matching source or create it below.
money.importExtensionSourceStep1: Open {source} and go to your transaction history (we can open it when you click Start import).
money.importExtensionSourceStep2: Click Start import and we'll create a session and open {source} if needed.
money.importExtensionSourceStep3: On the opened {source} page, click the visible Run import button and watch progress there.
money.noAccountsHint: Add an account to start tracking transactions.
money.ruleTargetCategoryHint: Only direct rules set a fixed category. Smart rules choose it automatically.
money.ruleMatchModeHint: All filters means every filter must match. Any filter means one match is enough.
money.ruleKindHint: Choose whether the rule sets a category directly or computes it automatically.
money.ruleKindTipdirect: Use direct rules when you already know the exact target category. The rule only changes a category when its filters and scope allow it.
money.ruleKindTipmcc_map: Uses the transaction MCC code and the built-in MCC mapping table to choose a canonical category automatically.
money.ruleKindTipsource_category_map: Uses the source category from the bank or importer and maps it to a canonical category automatically.
money.ruleKindTipllm_categorization: Sends the selected line item, transaction context, and available categories to the money-categorize Edge Function. It can pick a category or decide to leave the item unchanged.
money.ruleKindTipfallback_uncategorized: Runs near the end of the pipeline and assigns a built-in canonical fallback category when nothing better matched.
money.ruleScopeTipall_line_items: No scope restriction. The rule may run for any line item.
money.ruleScopeTipuncategorized_only: The rule only runs when the current line item still has no category.
money.ruleScopeTipcustom_only: The rule only runs when the current category is a custom category.
money.ruleScopeTipcanonical_only: The rule only runs when the current category is already canonical.
money.ruleScopeTipmanual_unlocked_only: The rule only runs for items that are not manually locked by a user.
money.rulePromptHint: Describe how the model should classify the item. The model receives the transaction, the line item, and the available categories.
money.ruleFallbackTargetHint: Pick the built-in canonical category to use when this fallback rule fires.
money.ruleFiltersHint: Filters are optional. Leave the list empty if this rule should be allowed to run for every line item in the selected scope.
money.ruleNoFiltersHint: No filters added. This rule can run for all line items that pass the selected scope filter.
money.ruleOperatorTipregex: The pattern must be a valid regular expression.
money.ruleOperatorTipin_set: Write a comma-separated list, for example: groceries, restaurant, coffee.
money.ruleOperatorTipcontains_any_in_set: Matches when the field contains any comma-separated value, for example: coffee, market, taxi.
money.ruleOperatorTipequals_any_in_set: Matches when the field exactly equals one comma-separated value, for example: groceries, restaurant, coffee.
money.ruleOperatorTiprange: Min and max are inclusive. You can use negative numbers, zero, or decimals.
money.ruleEnabledHint: Disabled rules stay in the list but are skipped by the pipeline.
money.ruleStopProcessing: Stop after this rule changes a category
money.ruleStopProcessingHint: When enabled, later rules will not run after this rule changes the category. Use it when this rule should win immediately.
money.ruleQuickActionsHint: These actions run the full pipeline, not just one rule. Use the standalone editor to preview a single rule on a real transaction.
money.ruleReplayReviewHint: Run the full categorization pipeline and keep a detailed report of what changed for each affected line item.
money.ruleReplayReviewIndexHint: Replay and review now lives in a dedicated workspace so date-range runs can keep a full per-line report.
money.ruleForceOverwriteLockedHint: Only enable this when you intentionally want rules to replace categories that were locked manually.
money.ruleExampleHint: Pick a real transaction and one line item to understand how this single rule behaves.
money.ruleExampleLineItemHint: Choose the exact line item the rule should be tested against.
money.ruleExampleNoLineItems: This transaction has no line items to test with.
money.ruleExampleCreateTipBody: New rules are previewed after the first save because the backend needs a real rule id before it can run a single-rule example.
money.ruleExampleDirtyTipBody: The current preview reflects the last saved version of the rule. Save again to refresh the example with your latest edits.
money.rulePreviewSingleRuleHint: This panel shows only the selected rule on the chosen example line item.
money.rulePreviewEmpty: Run a preview to inspect the next category decision.
money.ruleReportEmpty: Run a preview or replay to inspect success, failures, and category changes.
money.ruleRunReportOnlyUnmappedHint: Show only runs that still ended without a mapped category.
money.ruleRunReportNoFilteredResults: No runs match the current filters.
money.rulePipelineErrorMissingLineItem: The selected line item is no longer available. Choose another line item and try again.
money.rulePipelineErrorMissingTransaction: The selected transaction is no longer available. Choose another transaction and try again.
money.rulePipelineErrorLlmUnavailable: LLM rule preview is unavailable because OPENROUTER_API_KEY is not configured for the local money-categorize function.
money.rulePipelineErrorTimeout: The rule pipeline timed out before it could finish. Try again, or check the local money-categorize function logs.
money.rulePipelineErrorUnauthorized: The rule pipeline request is not authenticated. Sign in again and retry.
money.rulePipelineErrorGeneric: The rule pipeline could not run. Check the selected transaction or line item and try again.
money.rulePipelineErrorDateRange: The rule replay could not run for that date range. Check the dates and try again.
money.ruleSummaryNoFilters: Applies to all line items that pass the selected scope.
money.ruleValidationTargetRequired: Direct rules need a target category.
money.ruleValidationRegexInvalid: The regex filter is not valid.
money.ruleValidationDateRangeRequired: Choose both start and end dates.
money.ruleExampleTransactionRequired: Choose a transaction and line item first.
money.ruleNoLineItemSelected: Select a line item to inspect categorization history.
money.noRulesHint: Create the first rule for the selected person.
money.importNoAccounts: No {source} accounts. Add an account first.
money.importNoAccountsTooltip: There are no accounts for {source}. Add one with the matching source or create it below.
money.importExtensionGuide: Open the source website, authorize if needed, then run import directly on that page. Use popup only for debugging/fallback.
money.importExtensionStep1: Open T-Bank and go to your operations (we can open it when you click Start import).
money.importExtensionStep2: Click Start import — we'll create a session and open T-Bank if needed.
money.importExtensionStep3: On the opened T-Bank page, click the visible Run import button and watch progress there.
money.importExtensionInstallDev: Load the extension from the dev build: run the build script, then in Chrome go to Extensions в†’ Developer mode в†’ Load unpacked and select the browserExtension output folder.
money.importExtensionInstallProd: Download the latest production extension package and install it in Chrome.
money.importExtensionInstallProdStep1: Download the latest ZIP package from this page.
money.importExtensionInstallProdStep2: In Chrome open Extensions, enable Developer mode, then extract the ZIP and click Load unpacked.
money.importExtensionInstallProdStep3: Select the extracted extension folder, reload this page, then click Retry check.
money.importExtensionReloadHint: After installing the extension, reload this page, then click Retry check.
money.importExtensionUpdateAvailable: A newer extension build is available. Download it before the next import.
money.importExtensionSessionCreated: Session created. Open your T-Bank tab and click the visible Run import button on the page.
money.importExtensionSessionStarted: Session started. Continue in extension popup.
money.importExtensionOpenPopupManual: If on-page flow is unavailable, open extension popup and start processing there (debug fallback).
money.importHistoryEmptyHint: Import batches for the selected person will appear here.
money.importPendingReviewBanner: This report is a preview. Review the predicted results, then choose whether to apply this batch. Final apply results can differ if the underlying data changed.
money.importDiscardedBanner: This batch was reviewed and not applied. The report is kept for audit purposes.
